exposure: Antibiotic exposures during pregnancy and early childhood
outcome: Gut bacterial microbiota development (alpha and beta diversity)
cohort: 60 children from a rural tropical district in coastal Ecuador, followed from early infancy to 5 years of age.
finding: Children in a non-industrialized setting living in conditions of greater poverty and typically rural exposures, including consumption of unpasteurized milk, appeared to acquire a more rapidly stable and diverse gut bacterial microbiome during childhood.
mod_finding: Delivery method appeared to have limited effects on developmental trajectories of gut microbiota.
